physical.title: cape
physical.summary:
Kipuka (cape), trapezoidal in shape, consisting of white, black and golden-brown chicken feathers as well as red ʻapapane feathers, some red ʻiʻiwi feathers and yellow ōʻō feathers, still attached to bird skin.  
The upper panel of the kipuka is comprised of a layer of olonā matting, onto which bird skins with feathers attached have been stitched. The feathers are mostly red (likely ʻapapane) with a row of yellow feathers, also on bird skins (possibly ōʻō or mamo) along the bottom edge of the mat.  
The lower part of the kipuka consists of a central panel of white chicken feathers, many of which have been trimmed so the feather ends in two points. There are bands of black chicken feathers above and below the central panel and broad bands of golden-brown chicken feathers on either side. The feathers are tied in bundles to a groundwork of olonā fibre nae (net).  
Both the mat and nae are tied to a thick plaited olonā fibre cord that runs along the top of the kipuka and a thinner cord that runs along the sides. At the corners of the neckline the cords are plaited together and extend beyond the neckline to become ties. At the bottom of the kipuka the cords turn back on themselves and create loops.
